questions.question: A car with a mass of 150 kg is moving at a speed of 36 km/hr. What is the amount of work required to increase its speed to 72 km/hr?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**22,500 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The work required to increase the speed of the car can be calculated using the **work-energy theorem**, which states that the work done on an object is equal to the change in its kinetic energy.
 
• The formula for kinetic energy is given as: **K.E. = (1/2)mv²**, where **m** is the mass of the object and **v** is its velocity.
 
• The initial speed of the car is **36 km/hr**, which needs to be converted into meters per second: **36 km/hr = 36 × (1000 / 3600) = 10 m/s**.
 
• The final speed of the car is **72 km/hr**, which is converted into meters per second: **72 km/hr = 72 × (1000 / 3600) = 20 m/s**.
 
• Using the kinetic energy formula, calculate the initial kinetic energy: **K.E. initial = (1/2) × 150 × (10)² = 7500 J**.
 
• Calculate the final kinetic energy: **K.E. final = (1/2) × 150 × (20)² = 30,000 J**.
 
• The work done (or energy required) to increase the speed is the difference in kinetic energies: **Work = K.E. final - K.E. initial = 30,000 J - 7500 J = 22,500 J**.
 
• Therefore, the correct amount of work required is **22,500 J**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kinetic Energy:**

 
 
• Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by an object due to its motion.
 
• The formula for kinetic energy is: **K.E. = (1/2)mv²**, where **m** is the mass and **v** is the velocity.
 
• It is measured in **joules (J)**, the SI unit of energy.
 
 
 
• **Work-Energy Theorem:**
 
 
• The work-energy theorem states that the net work done on an object is equal to the change in its kinetic energy.
 
• This principle is crucial for solving problems involving the relationship between work and energy.
 
 
 
• **Conversion of Units:**
 
 
• Speed is often given in **km/hr**, but for physics calculations, it must be converted to **m/s**.
 
• The conversion factor is: **1 km/hr = (1000 / 3600) m/s**.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications:**
 
 
• Understanding work and energy principles is essential for engineering tasks such as calculating the energy required to accelerate vehicles.
 
• This concept is also used in designing engines, braking systems, and safety measures in automobiles.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Work:**

 
 
• Work is the transfer of energy that occurs when a force is applied over a distance.
 
• Formula: **Work = Force × Distance × cos(θ)**, where **θ** is the angle between the force and displacement direction.
 
 
 
• **Energy Conservation:**
 
 
• The principle of energy conservation states that energy cannot be created or destroyed but can only be transformed from one form to another.
 
• In this case, mechanical energy (kinetic energy) is increased by doing work on the car.
 
 
 
• **SI Units:**
 
 
• Energy is measured in **joules (J)**, and 1 joule is equivalent to 1 newton-meter (N·m).
 
• Speed is measured in **meters per second (m/s)**, and mass is measured in **kilograms (kg)**.

questions.question: Which of the following is an enzyme that is secreted in the stomach during the process of digestion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pepsin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pepsin** is a digestive enzyme that is secreted by the stomach, specifically from the gastric glands located in the lining of the stomach.
 
• Pepsin is secreted in an inactive form called **pepsinogen**. Pepsinogen is activated into pepsin by hydrochloric acid (HCl) present in the stomach.
 
• **Function of Pepsin:** It plays a critical role in breaking down proteins into smaller peptides during the process of digestion. Proteins are complex molecules, and pepsin facilitates their breakdown into more digestible forms.
 
• **Location:** Pepsin activity occurs in the highly acidic environment of the stomach, where the pH is around 1.5-3.5. This acidic condition is essential for its optimal functioning.
 
• **Importance:** Pepsin is one of the first enzymes to initiate the digestion of dietary proteins. Without it, protein digestion would be significantly impaired.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mucus:**

 
 
• Mucus is secreted by the stomach lining but it is not an enzyme. It serves as a protective layer to prevent the stomach lining from being damaged by the acidic gastric juice and digestive enzymes.
 
• Its primary function is protection rather than digestion.
 
 
 
• **Amylase:**
 
 
• Amylase is a carbohydrate-digesting enzyme that is secreted by the salivary glands and pancreas, not the stomach.
 
• It breaks down starch into simpler sugars like maltose.
 
• Amylase does not function in the acidic environment of the stomach. It is active in the mouth and small intestine.
 
 
 
• **Trypsin:**
 
 
• Trypsin is a protein-digesting enzyme secreted by the pancreas in an inactive form called trypsinogen.
 
• It becomes active in the small intestine and aids in further digestion of proteins after pepsin has initiated the process in the stomach.
 
• It does not play a role in digestion within the stomach.
 
 
 
• **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl):**
 
 
• HCl is secreted by the parietal cells in the stomach lining. It creates an acidic environment that is essential for the activation and functioning of pepsin.
 
• It helps in killing harmful bacteria present in food and denaturing proteins for easier digestion.
 
 
 
• **Protein Digestion:**
 
 
• The process of protein digestion starts in the stomach with pepsin and is completed in the small intestine with enzymes like trypsin and chymotrypsin.
 
• The breakdown of proteins is essential for the absorption of amino acids, which are the building blocks for various bodily functions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Stomach Enzymes:** The stomach primarily secretes pepsin for protein digestion, but it also produces other components like mucus and hydrochloric acid for maintaining digestion and protecting the stomach lining.
 
• **Pepsinogen Activation:** The activation of pepsinogen into pepsin is a self-regulating process that ensures enzyme activity occurs only when needed, preventing damage to the stomach lining.
 
• **pH Dependency:** Pepsin requires a very low pH to function effectively. This is why the stomach environment is highly acidic, maintained by hydrochloric acid secretion.
 
• **Role in Overall Digestion:** While pepsin works in the stomach, other enzymes like amylase and trypsin function in different parts of the digestive system, ensuring comprehensive digestion of food.

questions.question: A student cannot clearly see objects placed at a distance but can read a book comfortably. The defect in the eye is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Myopia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Myopia**, also known as **near-sightedness**, is a common vision defect where an individual can see nearby objects clearly but struggles to view distant objects.
 
• This condition occurs when the **eyeball is elongated** or the **cornea is too curved**, causing light rays to focus in front of the retina instead of directly on it.
 
• Myopia can be corrected using **concave lenses**, which help redirect light rays to focus correctly on the retina.
 
• The primary symptom of myopia is **blurry vision for distant objects**, while near vision remains unaffected.
 
• It commonly develops during **childhood or adolescence** and may worsen with age if not managed properly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Presbyopia:**

 
 
• Presbyopia is an age-related vision defect that typically develops around the age of **40**, causing difficulty in focusing on close objects.
 
• This condition occurs due to the **loss of elasticity in the lens** of the eye, making it harder to focus on nearby objects.
 
• Presbyopia is corrected using **convex lenses** or bifocal lenses.
 
• Unlike myopia, presbyopia is not caused by the shape of the eyeball but by the natural aging process.
 
 
 
• **Hypermetropia:**
 
 
• Also known as **far-sightedness**, hypermetropia is a defect where distant objects are seen clearly, but nearby objects appear blurry.
 
• This occurs when the **eyeball is too short** or the **lens is too flat**, causing light rays to focus behind the retina.
 
• Hypermetropia can be corrected using **convex lenses**, which help light rays focus directly on the retina.
 
• It is more common in children and may improve with age as the eyeball grows.
 
 
 
• **Astigmatism:**
 
 
• Astigmatism is a vision defect caused by an **irregularly shaped cornea** or lens, leading to distorted or blurred vision at all distances.
 
• This condition causes light rays to focus on multiple points on the retina instead of a single point.
 
• Astigmatism can be corrected with **cylindrical lenses** or through surgical procedures like LASIK.
 
• It can occur in combination with myopia or hypermetropia.
 
 
 
• **Important Characteristics of Myopia:**
 
 
• Myopia is often genetic but can also be influenced by **environmental factors** such as prolonged near work (e.g., reading or using digital devices).
 
• It is diagnosed through an **eye examination** that includes testing visual acuity and refraction.
 
• Severe cases of myopia, known as **high myopia**, may increase the risk of complications such as **retinal detachment** or glaucoma.
 
• Myopia management strategies, such as **orthokeratology lenses** or atropine eye drops, are used to slow the progression of the condition in children.

questions.question: In the process of sexual reproduction in flowering plants, what is the primary role of the pistil?

The correct answer is __**Receives pollen and houses the ovules for fertilisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **pistil** is the female reproductive part of a flowering plant. It consists of three main structures: the **stigma**, **style**, and **ovary**, each of which plays a crucial role in reproduction.
 
• The **stigma**, located at the top of the pistil, is sticky and serves as the site where **pollen grains are received**.
 
• The **style** is the tube-like structure that connects the stigma to the ovary. It facilitates the movement of the **pollen tube** down to the ovary for fertilisation.
 
• Inside the **ovary** are ovules, which house the **female gametes**. After successful fertilisation, these ovules develop into seeds.
 
• The primary role of the pistil is to **enable fertilisation** by providing a structure for the **pollen to reach the ovules**, ensuring the development of seeds and fruits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Functions of the Pistil:**

 
 
• **Receiving Pollen:** The stigma is specially adapted to trap and hold pollen grains for fertilisation.
 
• **Facilitating Fertilisation:** The style provides a pathway for the pollen tube to grow and reach the ovary.
 
• **Seed Formation:** Post-fertilisation, the ovules in the ovary develop into seeds, and the ovary matures into fruit.
 
 
 
• **Role of Other Flower Structures:**
 
 
• **Petals:** Brightly coloured to attract pollinators like bees and butterflies.
 
• **Sepals:** Protect the flower bud before it blooms.
 
• **Stamens:** Male reproductive parts that produce and release pollen grains.
 
 
 
• **Pollination:**
 
 
• **Self-pollination:** Pollen from the anther of a flower lands on the stigma of the same flower or another flower on the same plant.
 
• **Cross-pollination:** Pollen is transferred from the anther of one plant's flower to the stigma of another plant's flower, increasing genetic diversity.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Flowering Plants:**
 
 
• **Monocots:** Maize, rice, wheat (single cotyledon).
 
• **Dicots:** Rose, sunflower, mango (two cotyledons).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Stigma Adaptations:** The stigma can be sticky or feathery, depending on whether the plant relies on insect or wind pollination.
 
• **Pollination Agents:** Pollination can occur through biotic agents like insects and birds or abiotic agents like wind and water.
 
• **Fertilisation Process:** After the pollen tube reaches the ovule, sperm cells are released, and one of them fuses with the egg cell to form a zygote.
 
• **Seed Dispersal:** Post-fertilisation, seeds are dispersed via wind, water, animals, or mechanical means to ensure plant propagation.

questions.question: What type of bonding exists in most organic compounds?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Covalent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Covalent bonding** is the primary type of bonding in **most organic compounds**. It involves the sharing of electrons between atoms to form stable molecules.
 
• **Organic compounds** are primarily composed of **carbon (C), hydrogen (H), oxygen (O), nitrogen (N), and other nonmetals**. These elements tend to form covalent bonds because of their electronegativity and need to complete their valence shell.
 
• Covalent bonds allow the formation of complex molecular structures, such as **chains, rings, and branches**, which are characteristic of organic compounds.
 
• Examples of organic compounds with covalent bonding include **methane (CH₄), ethanol (C₂H₅OH), and glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆)**.
 
• **Single, double, and triple covalent bonds** are common in organic molecules, depending on the number of electrons shared between atoms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Coordinate Bonding**:

 
 
• A coordinate bond involves one atom donating a pair of electrons to another atom. It is often seen in **complexes** or **inorganic compounds**, such as in ammonia-boron trifluoride (NH₃-BF₃).
 
• Organic compounds rarely exhibit coordinate bonding, except in specific cases involving metal-organic complexes.
 
 
 
• **Ionic Bonding**:
 
 
• Ionic bonding occurs when electrons are transferred from one atom to another, resulting in oppositely charged ions. This is typical in compounds like **NaCl** and **MgO**.
 
• Organic compounds rarely exhibit ionic bonding. However, ionic interactions may occur in salts of organic acids or bases, such as **sodium acetate (CH₃COONa)**.
 
 
 
• **Metallic Bonding**:
 
 
• Metallic bonding is present in metals where valence electrons form a "sea of electrons" around positive metal ions. This type of bonding is responsible for properties like **conductivity** and **malleability** in metals.
 
• Organic compounds do not exhibit metallic bonding as they are composed of nonmetals.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Organic Molecules:**
 
 
• **Hydrocarbons**: Methane (CH₄), Ethene (C₂H₄), Ethyne (C₂H₂).
 
• **Functional Groups**: Alcohols (C₂H₅OH), Aldehydes (HCHO), and Ketones (CH₃COCH₃).
 
• **Biomolecules**: Glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆), Amino Acids, and Lipids.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nature of Organic Compounds**: Organic chemistry deals with compounds containing **carbon**. Carbon's ability to form four covalent bonds makes it uniquely suited for creating diverse and complex molecular structures.
 
• **Types of Covalent Bonds**: Organic molecules may contain **single bonds (alkanes), double bonds (alkenes), or triple bonds (alkynes)**. These bonds significantly influence the chemical properties and reactivity of the molecules.
 
• **Applications of Organic Compounds**: Organic compounds are used in **pharmaceuticals**, **polymers**, **fuels**, and **agriculture**. For example, ethanol serves as a solvent and fuel, while glucose is vital for biological energy.
 
• **Functional Groups**: Functional groups like **-OH (hydroxyl), -COOH (carboxyl), and -NH₂ (amino)** confer specific properties to organic molecules, enabling a wide range of applications in chemistry and biology.
 
• **Importance of Covalent Bonding**: Covalent bonds allow the creation of stable and versatile molecules necessary for life and various industries. The ability of carbon to form covalent bonds is the foundation of organic chemistry.

questions.question: The method of extraction of a metal depends on its:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Position in the reactivity series**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **method of extraction of a metal** is primarily determined by its **position in the reactivity series**, which categorizes metals based on their chemical reactivity.
 
• Metals **low in the reactivity series**, such as gold and silver, are often found in their **native state** and require minimal extraction processes like physical separation or amalgamation.
 
• Metals in the **middle of the reactivity series**, like zinc and iron, are usually found in the form of **oxides, sulfides, or carbonates**. These metals are extracted using processes like **reduction with carbon or carbon monoxide** in a blast furnace.
 
• Highly reactive metals such as sodium, potassium, and aluminum, found at the **top of the reactivity series**, are extracted using **electrolysis**. These metals form very stable compounds, and electrolysis is necessary to break these bonds.
 
• The **reactivity series** provides a systematic way to predict how metals react with water, acids, and other substances, which directly influences the **extraction method**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reactivity Series:**

 
 
• The reactivity series is a list of metals arranged in order of decreasing reactivity.
 
• Highly reactive metals like **potassium, sodium, and calcium** are at the top, while **gold and platinum**, which are unreactive, are at the bottom.
 
• The series helps determine whether a metal can displace another metal from its compound, which is crucial in choosing the right extraction method.
 
 
 
• **Extraction Processes:**
 
 
• **Electrolysis:** Used for highly reactive metals like aluminum, where electricity breaks down compounds into their elements.
 
• **Reduction with carbon:** Used for moderately reactive metals like iron. The metal oxide is reduced to the metal by heating with carbon.
 
• **Physical methods:** For less reactive metals like gold, where methods like panning or amalgamation are sufficient.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Metals:**
 
 
• **Sodium and Potassium:** Extracted using electrolysis due to their high reactivity.
 
• **Zinc and Iron:** Extracted using reduction with carbon or carbon monoxide.
 
• **Gold and Silver:** Found in native form and extracted using physical methods.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Reactivity Series:**
 
 
• Predicting the outcome of displacement reactions.
 
• Identifying suitable methods for metal extraction.
 
• Understanding the corrosion behavior of metals.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mass Number:** The mass number of a metal is unrelated to its extraction process. It refers to the sum of protons and neutrons in an atom.
 
• **Atomic Number:** The atomic number, which indicates the number of protons in the nucleus, is also not directly related to the extraction method.
 
• **Colour:** The color of a metal does not influence its extraction technique. It is a physical property unrelated to chemical reactivity.
 
• **Reactivity Series:** This is the primary determinant of the extraction process, as it reflects the chemical stability of the metal compounds.

questions.question: Which non-metal exhibits a lustrous shine like metals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iodine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

White light is incident obliquely on a glass prism, which of the following statement(s) is/are true?

(i) Red colour undergoes maximum deviation.

(ii) The speed of violet colour is the least while travelling through the prism.

(iii) The refractive index of violet is minimum.

(iv) The refractive index of red is minimum.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (ii) and (iv)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement (i):** Red colour undergoes maximum deviation.

 This statement is **incorrect**. Red light undergoes the **least deviation** because it has the longest wavelength among visible light, and deviation is inversely proportional to the wavelength in a prism.
 
• **Statement (ii):** The speed of violet colour is the least while travelling through the prism.

 This statement is **correct**. Violet light has the shortest wavelength and thus experiences the **maximum interaction with the prism material**, leading to its speed being the slowest.
 
• **Statement (iii):** The refractive index of violet is minimum.

 This statement is **incorrect**. The refractive index of a material is higher for shorter wavelengths. Since violet has the shortest wavelength, its refractive index is the **highest**.
 
• **Statement (iv):** The refractive index of red is minimum.

 This statement is **correct**. Red light, having the longest wavelength, has the **lowest refractive index** as it interacts least with the prism material.
 
• In a glass prism, due to the phenomenon of dispersion, white light splits into its constituent colours (VIBGYOR). Each colour bends differently because of varying refractive indices, and violet deviates the most while red deviates the least.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dispersion of Light:**

 
 
• Dispersion occurs when white light passes through a prism and splits into its constituent colours due to **variation in refractive indices** for different wavelengths.
 
• The order of colours observed is Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, and Red (VIBGYOR).
 
 
 
• **Refractive Index and Wavelength:**
 
 
• The refractive index of a medium is inversely proportional to the wavelength of light.
 
• Shorter wavelengths (e.g., violet) have higher refractive indices, causing more deviation.
 
• Longer wavelengths (e.g., red) have lower refractive indices, causing less deviation.
 
 
 
• **Prism and Deviation:**
 
 
• A prism bends light due to the phenomenon of refraction.
 
• The angle of deviation depends on the **wavelength of light** and the material of the prism.
 
• Violet light, being of shorter wavelength, deviates the most, while red light deviates the least.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Dispersion:**
 
 
• Dispersion helps in the formation of **rainbows** when sunlight passes through water droplets.
 
• Prisms are used in spectrometers to study the spectrum of light.
 
 
 
• **Important Values:**
 
 
• The refractive index of glass is typically higher for violet (around 1.53) and lower for red (around 1.51).
 
• The speed of light in a material is given by: **v = c/n**, where **c** is the speed of light in a vacuum, and **n** is the refractive index.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Wavelength and Colour:**

 
 
• The wavelength of violet light is approximately 400 nm, whereas red light has a wavelength of around 700 nm.
 
• The difference in wavelength leads to different speeds and refractive indices for various colours in a medium.
 
 
 
• **Deviation and Spectrum:**
 
 
• Deviation in a prism is caused by the change in speed of light as it enters and exits the prism.
 
• The visible spectrum observed after dispersion provides insights into the properties of light and the material of the prism.

questions.question: Which of the following can be considered a reason for Mendel's success in formulating laws of inheritance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**He had knowledge of mathematics.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gregor Johann Mendel**, known as the "Father of Genetics," successfully formulated the laws of inheritance by applying his knowledge of **mathematics and probability** to biology, which was a groundbreaking approach during his time.
 
• His use of **statistical methods** in analyzing the inheritance patterns of traits in pea plants provided a quantitative foundation for his conclusions, making his work highly reliable.
 
• Mendel conducted **controlled experiments**, such as cross-pollination of pea plants, and meticulously recorded data over multiple generations, demonstrating his analytical and mathematical prowess.
 
• He applied the principles of **ratios** and **probability** to predict and explain the occurrence of dominant and recessive traits, which later formed the basis of Mendel's laws: the Law of Segregation and the Law of Independent Assortment.
 
• While Mendel was a monk and not a formally trained scientist, his knowledge of mathematics was instrumental in ensuring the accuracy and reproducibility of his experiments, highlighting the importance of interdisciplinary knowledge in scientific discoveries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gregor Mendel’s Background:**

 
 
• Mendel was born in **1822 in Heinzendorf, Austria** (modern-day Czech Republic) and joined a monastery in **1843**.
 
• While at the monastery, he studied **mathematics and natural sciences** at the University of Vienna, which greatly influenced his scientific approach.
 
 
 
• **Pea Plant Experiments:**
 
 
• Mendel chose **pea plants** (Pisum sativum) for his experiments because they have distinct traits (e.g., flower color, seed shape) and can be easily controlled for cross-pollination.
 
• He studied **seven traits**, each with two contrasting forms, such as tall vs. short plants and round vs. wrinkled seeds.
 
 
 
• **Mendel’s Laws of Inheritance:**
 
 
• **Law of Segregation:** Alleles (gene variants) separate during gamete formation, and each gamete receives one allele.
 
• **Law of Independent Assortment:** Genes for different traits assort independently during gamete formation, provided they are not linked.
 
 
 
• **Rediscovery of Mendel’s Work:**
 
 
• Mendel’s research was largely ignored during his lifetime. His work was rediscovered in **1900** by three scientists: **Hugo de Vries, Carl Correns, and Erich von Tschermak.**
 
• Today, Mendel’s principles are the foundation of **modern genetics**, including fields like molecular biology and genetic engineering.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Mathematics in Biology:**
 
 
• Mendel’s use of mathematics demonstrated the potential of **quantitative methods** in biology, paving the way for biostatistics and computational biology.
 
• His statistical approach enabled accurate predictions of trait inheritance, which remain fundamental to understanding **genetic probabilities**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option 1: He had supernatural power:** This is incorrect. Mendel’s success was due to his scientific methodology and mathematical analysis, not any supernatural ability.
 
• **Option 2: He was a monk:** While Mendel was a monk, this fact was incidental and not the reason for his scientific success.
 
• **Option 3: He had knowledge of mathematics:** This is the correct answer, as Mendel’s application of mathematical principles was pivotal in formulating the laws of inheritance.
 
• **Option 4: He was a well-trained scientist:** Although Mendel studied sciences, he was not formally recognized as a trained scientist during his time.

questions.question: A gun fires a bullet horizontally. Which of the following statements is correct?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The gun experiences a backward force equal to the forward force on the bullet.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton’s Third Law of Motion**: According to Newton’s third law, for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. When the gun fires a bullet, the bullet moves forward with a certain force, and the gun experiences an equal and opposite force backward. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **Recoil of the Gun**: The backward movement of the gun is called recoil. This happens because the gun experiences a backward force equal to the forward force exerted on the bullet.
 
• **Momentum Conservation**: The firing of the bullet is an example of the law of conservation of momentum. Initially, the total momentum of the system (gun + bullet) is zero. After firing, the forward momentum of the bullet is equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the backward momentum of the gun. This ensures the total momentum remains conserved.
 
• **Force Exerted on Gun and Bullet**: The force exerted on the bullet by the gun is equal in magnitude to the force exerted on the gun by the bullet, as per Newton's third law. *Hence, statement 4 is correct.*
 
• **Irrelevance of Gravity**: Recoil is a result of forces acting within the system (gun and bullet) and is independent of external factors like gravity. *Hence, the statement "Recoil depends on gravity" is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton’s Third Law of Motion**:

 
 
• It states that if an object A exerts a force on object B, then object B simultaneously exerts a force of equal magnitude and in the opposite direction on object A.
 
• This principle underlies many physical interactions, including the recoil of guns, the propulsion of rockets, and even walking, where the feet push against the ground.
 
 
 
• **Conservation of Momentum**:
 
 
• The law of conservation of momentum states that the total momentum of a closed system remains constant, provided no external forces act on it.
 
• In the case of a gun firing a bullet, the forward momentum of the bullet is balanced by the backward momentum of the gun to conserve the total momentum of the system.
 
 
 
• **Recoil Velocity**:
 
 
• The recoil velocity of the gun can be calculated using the formula:

 **v_g = -(m_b × v_b) / m_g**

 where **v_g** is the gun's recoil velocity, **m_b** is the bullet's mass, **v_b** is the bullet's velocity, and **m_g** is the gun's mass.
 
• This formula shows that the heavier the gun, the smaller the recoil velocity for a given bullet momentum.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Newton’s Third Law**:
 
 
• **Rocket Propulsion**: Rockets work on the principle of Newton’s third law. The ejected gases exert a backward force, and the rocket moves forward due to the equal and opposite reaction force.
 
• **Firearms**: The recoil experienced when a gun is fired is a direct consequence of Newton’s third law.
 
• **Swimming**: When a swimmer pushes water backward with their hands, the water exerts an equal and opposite force, propelling them forward.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Incorrect Statements in the Question:**

 
 
• **“The bullet exerts no force on the gun”**: Incorrect because the bullet exerts an equal and opposite force on the gun as per Newton's third law.
 
• **“The gun experiences a smaller backward force”**: Incorrect because the gun experiences a force equal in magnitude to the bullet’s forward force.
 
• **“Recoil depends on gravity”**: Incorrect because recoil is an internal force within the system and is not influenced by gravity.

Pipe P can fill (4)/(5) part of a tank in 28 hours and pipe Q can fill (2)/(3) part of the same tank in 42 hours. Both P and Q were kept open for 7 hours, then both were closed. Pipe R alone was then opened and it emptied the water in the tank in 14 hours.

Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time for P = 28 × 5/4 = 35 hours; Time for Q = 42 × 3/2 = 63 hours.

LCM(35, 63) = 315 units (Total Work).

Efficiency: P = 9, Q = 5.

Filled in 7 hours = (9 + 5) × 7 = 98 units.

R efficiency = 98 ÷ 14 = 7 units/hr (emptying).

Net efficiency (P+Q−R) = 9 + 5 − 7 = 7 units/hr.

Required time = 315 ÷ 7 = 45 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 45 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given: **

P fills 4/5 in 28 hrs, Q fills 2/3 in 42 hrs, R empties filled part in 14 hrs after 7 hrs.

Total Work = Efficiency × Time;

Efficiency of filling pipe is positive, emptying is negative.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Full time for P = 28 × (5 ÷ 4) = 35 hours

⇒ Full time for Q = 42 × (3 ÷ 2) = 63 hours

⇒ Let Total Work = LCM(35, 63) = 315 units

⇒ Work done by P and Q in 7 hours = 7 × (Efficiency of P + Efficiency of Q)

⇒ Work done = 7 × (9 + 5) = 98 units

⇒ Efficiency of R = Work ÷ Time = 98 ÷ 14 = 7 units/hr (negative work)

⇒ Time for R to empty full tank = 315 ÷ 7 = 45 hours

questions.question: Which lake, known as India’s longest and a Ramsar site in Kerala is currently facing severe ecological degradation?
